newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh's 1996 rice output may be record - FAO.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh's 1996 rice output may be record - FAO.

text.p: Bangladesh may have produced a record 29.1 million tonnes of paddy (unmilled rice) in 1996, when total output of milled rice is expected to exceed 20 million tonnes, an official with the Food and Agricuture Organisation (FAO) said on Thursday.

"We visited remote areas of the country and were surprised to see the abundance of crops in fields. The production may break the all-time record," said Dr. M. A. Ashraf, a programme officer at the FAO office in Dhaka.
"The total output of paddy is likely to reach 29.1 million tonnes, up 9.34 percent from 26.57 million tonnes in 1995," he said.
Ashraf referred to FAO's "Rice Market Update" which he said showed that Bangladesh achieved a tremendous success in producing its 1996 rice crop, better than Burma, Thailand and Vietnam.
The bumper harvest was attributed to excellent weather.
The FAO forecast Bangladesh's 1997 food import would drop to 400,000 tonnes from 500,000 in the past year.
Bangladesh has a population of around 120 million.
